tldr.text: This lesson takes the program beyond your own walls, to vendors, incidents and change. You can outsource the work but not the accountability. A vendor with your data or a login is part of your attack surface, and its suppliers matter too.

Manage each vendor across the whole relationship, from inventory and tiering through due diligence, contract and monitoring to offboarding. Tier by the data, access and dependence a vendor carries, never by spend, and let the tier set the scrutiny.

When a vendor hands you a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate, read its scope, its period, its exceptions and the controls it leaves to you. Questionnaires and security ratings help, but neither is the whole answer. End in a recorded decision.
tldr.say: When a vendor hands you a sock two report or an I S O twenty-seven thousand one certificate, read its scope, its period, its exceptions and the controls it leaves to you. Questionnaires and security ratings help, but neither is the whole answer. End in a recorded decision.

tldr.text: An incident is when a risk on the register stops being hypothetical. After it is contained, re-rate the risk, turn each gap into an owned and dated action, update policy and vendors, track the metrics, and bring in legal and compliance early.

Every significant change, from an acquisition or a cloud migration to a new regulation or an AI feature, can make part of the program wrong. Build one question into existing processes. Does this change our scope, our risks or our controls?
tldr.say: Every significant change, from an acquisition or a cloud migration to a new regulation or an A I feature, can make part of the program wrong. Build one question into existing processes. Does this change our scope, our risks or our controls?

tldr.text: It all comes back to three questions. Who decided, what could go wrong, and can we show it? A mature program answers them for vendors, incidents and change as clearly as for its own controls.
Now try the exercises. Put the vendor lifecycle in order, place a few vendors in their tiers, and trace an incident back into the program. Then finish with the knowledge check.

activities.title: Walk a vendor through its lifecycle
activities.prompt: Big Venture is bringing on a new vendor that will hold employee data. Put the stages of the relationship in order.
steps: Record the vendor, its owner, the data it receives and the access it has
Rank it by criticality and by the data and access it holds
Assess its security with a questionnaire, reports and external signals
Sign a contract with security terms, breach notice and a right to audit
Reassess on the tier's cadence and track findings to closure
Revoke its access, get the data back or deleted, and update the inventory
activities.why: Tiering needs the facts the inventory records, and the tier sets how deep due diligence goes before the contract is signed. Monitoring runs for the life of the relationship, and offboarding closes the record the inventory opened.

activities.title: Tier the vendors
activities.prompt: Place each of Big Venture's vendors in the tier its data, access and dependence call for.

items.text: Cloud provider hosting the payroll platform
items.why: It holds sensitive data and has production access, and an outage would stop the service.

items.text: A free tool with broad access to production
items.why: Spend does not set the tier, and broad production access makes it critical.

items.text: A big-budget design agency with no data and no access
items.why: A large invoice does not raise the tier when there is no data, no access and the agency is easy to replace.

items.text: Support ticketing tool, with workarounds if it fails
items.why: It holds some sensitive data, but the business can work around an outage.

items.text: Printing firm that now receives employees' full bank details
items.why: Sensitive data puts it in the top tier, and its tier should have changed when the bank details started to flow.

items.text: Font license used by the marketing team
items.why: It holds no sensitive data, has no access and is easy to replace.

items.text: Project planning tool with internal access and a fallback if it fails
items.why: Internal access with a workaround puts it in the middle tier.

items.text: Stock photo subscription with no data and no access
items.why: Nothing sensitive flows to it and it could be swapped out easily.

activities.title: Read an incident back into the program
activities.prompt: Big Venture's ticketing vendor reports that an attacker used a stolen session to export attachments. Put the follow-up in order.
steps: The incident is detected and contained, and systems are recovered
A post-incident review establishes what failed, and why
The vendor data leak risk is re-rated and checked against appetite
Each gap becomes an owned, dated item in the corrective action plan
Evidence and metrics show whether the fixes work
Policy, playbooks and training are updated before the next incident
activities.why: The review has to establish what failed before the risk can be re-rated, and the new rating shows which gaps need actions. Evidence that the fixes work then updates preparation for the next incident, while legal and compliance review notification throughout.
